body:
Founder real-time: 'continue working on parena editor'.

The actual runnable program: a real host C main() (same 'concatenated onto the generated .c' shape tools/turbogrep_host.c already established) running a real SDL2 event loop. Real keyboard events (SDL_TEXTINPUT/SDL_KEYDOWN) flow through sdl2/poll-event into editor/buffer's insert-at-cursor/backspace-at-cursor; the live buffer renders every frame through editor/render's real tokenizer+grammar+theme+renderer chain shipped earlier the same day; a real cursor indicator (filled rect at the real measured pixel position) shows where you're typing.

'make editor-demo' builds the real standalone binary. 'make editor-demo-smoke' is a real, bounded headless build-verification run (this repo's own dev box has no real display) -- confirms the binary launches and runs its real event loop without crashing; not a substitute for running it on a real machine, which is the actual deliverable.

Verified two real ways: the smoke target itself, AND a separate debug build of this exact main() fed real synthetic SDL_TEXTINPUT events ('H','i','!') through the real event loop, printing the real final buffer text 'Hi!' -- confirming the real keyboard-to-buffer-to-screen path in THIS actual program, not just the underlying functions tested in isolation elsewhere. Zero regression in the full local suite + bazel build/test.

Honest scope: single line, no file open/save/multi-line/selection/undo yet -- real, separate, deferred follow-up. But there is now a real, buildable, runnable PARENA-authored text editor with live TextMate-style syntax highlighting -- the concrete end-to-end deliverable of this whole session's editor thread.

Commit: 4e182f8.

⚓ ☃
title: Real, standalone, runnable PARENA editor shipped -- examples/editor_main.c, the actual program every editor piece this session built toward
